sources.observation: Owned non-fork repositories include bat, fd, hyperfine, hexyl, pastel, numbat and other developer tools.
bat is a cross-platform cat-like CLI with syntax highlighting, Git integration, paging, terminal-context behavior and extensive integrations with other command-line tools.
hyperfine is a cross-platform command benchmarking tool with statistical analysis, warmups, cache preparation, outlier detection, parameterized benchmarks, calibration and result export.

Numbat is a statically typed scientific-computation language with physical dimensions as types, first-class units, strict syntax, error messages, REPL, extensible standard library and runtime assertions; README states the project is maintained by David Peter / sharkdp.
Recent 2026 repository history includes documentation-build optimization and continuing standard-library/tooling changes.

scope_boundaries: Owned projects support sustained project-level practice, not sole authorship of every contribution.
Using syntax-highlighting/Git/pager dependencies does not imply mastery of those external implementations.
Hyperfine's statistical features support benchmarking-tool design, not broad statistical research expertise.
Numbat supports language/tooling design evidence but does not by itself prove general compiler-theory mastery.
